sentences.text:
This appeal coming on for admission/orders this day, th  the following:
 JUDGEMENT 1] Heard finally with the consent of the parties.
2] This appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 19/07/2022, passed in Claim Case No.67/2020, registration No.128/2020 by First Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dardarpur, District Dhar (M.P.) seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

3] In brief, the facts of the case are that on 22/01/2020, at around 10:00 O'clock in the night, when the deceased Sanjay Vasuniya was going towards his home from Sardarpur to Badweli on his motorcycle, at that time, he met with an accident with a car baring registration No.GJ 10-AC 9224,
which was being driven rashly and negligently by the respondent no.1, as a result of which, the deceased Sanjay Vasuniya died on the spot only.

On account of death of Sanjay, his legal heirs filed a claim case No.67/2020 in the Court of MACT, Sardarpur, District Dhar, and the learned Tribunal after recording the evidence decided the claim case on 19/07/2022 and an award of Rs.12,47,500/-
was passed in favour of the appellants/claimants, and being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal has been preferred.
4] Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the award is on lower side and needs to be enhanced as the deceased was a skilled labour/mason and earning Rs.30,000/- per month, whereas the Tribunal has considered his income as Rs.5,000/- only, and apart from that, the future prospects of the deceased has been considered as 30% only instead of 40%.

In support of his submissions, shri Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellants has relied upon the judgement passed in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 ACJ Smt. Avanti vs Rais Khan on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25348886/
2 2700 (SC).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 ACJ Smt. Avanti vs Rais Khan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the award be enhanced appropriately.

5] Shri Manoj Jain, leanred counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the award is just and proper and no interference is called for.
6] Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7] On due consideration of submissions and on perusal of the record, this Court finds force in the submissions as advanced by the learned counsel for the appellants to some extent, and although the income of the deceased cannot be considered to be Rs.30,000/- per month, however, under the facts and circumstances of the case, by adopting a reasonable approach, it can be considered as Rs.7,000/- per month and accordingly while applying the ratio in the case of National Insurance Co.
Vs. Pranay Sethi (supra), this Court finds that the calculations vis- -vis the award passed by the claims tribunal can be made in the following manner:-
The calculation made by the claims Tribunal:-
Dependency [5000 + (30% of 5000)] X 1/4 X 12 9,94,500 X 17

National Insurance Co.
Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Filial
consortium
Funeral expenses 16,500
Loss of estate 16,500 Total 12,47,500

The calculation made by this Court is as under :-
 Dependency 7000 + 40% of 7000 (=2800) = 14,99,
 9800 - 9800 X 1/4 (2450) = 7350 X 12 = 88,200  X 17  Filial consortium 44000 X 5 2,20,0  Funeral expenses 16,50  Loss of estate 16,50  Total 17,52,
 Amount awarded by the Tribunal - 12,47,
 Amount to be enhanced 5,04,9  8] In view of the above, the appal stands partly allowed  that the appellants shall be entitled to receive an additional enhanced amount of Rs.5,04,900/- (rupees five lakhs four thousand nine hundred only) towards the compensation along with the interest as awarded by the tribunal.
It is also directed that the Court fees be refunded back to the appellants which has been paid by them in accordance with law.
9] Appeal stands disposed of.
(SUBODH ABHYAN  JU
